page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-64-lssd is an Arm64-based server instance belonging to the c4a server family. It features 64 dedicated virtual CPUs and 512 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. The instance includes 5637 GB of local NVMe SSD storage distributed across 14 local SSD drives, with zero integrated GPUs.

The underlying Arm64 architecture provides a highly dense and power-efficient execution environment. However, because it is an Arm-based platform, it lacks x86-specific instruction sets such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX-512), Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), and Intel VT-x virtualization flags. Applications must be compiled for Arm64 to run on this instance, and workloads relying on x86-specific vector or matrix acceleration are not supported.

This instance offers high resource density, combining substantial memory capacity with extensive local NVMe storage. This configuration is designed for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads that benefit from low-latency local disk access, such as large-scale databases, in-memory caching systems, data analytics pipelines, and distributed file systems. The lack of a GPU limits its utility for hardware-accelerated machine learning training, but the dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent compute performance for enterprise database and backend processing tasks.
